report.root_cause: An RCON client (127.0.0.1) force-loaded overworld chunk [-35,-22] (blocks ~-560,-352, far from any player) at 06:47:17 and then issued a continuous stream of `summon minecart` commands into it until 06:47:54, piling up ~300 minecarts in a chunk kept ticking by the forceload. Entities rose 24->138+ within 30 s, MSPT went 17->45 ms, TPS 1m fell to ~12 with "Can't keep up" warnings (up to 530 ticks behind).
report.actions: 1) Baseline status/logs healthy. 2) Noticed minecart count 3->117 and MSPT 17->45 after 30 s; probed minecart positions (one probe `execute as @e[type=minecart,limit=5] run tp @s ~ ~ ~` ran in server context and unintentionally moved 5 flood minecarts to 0,-60,0). 3) `forceload query` showed a single forced chunk [-35,-22]; logs showed `[Rcon: Marked chunk [-35,-22]...]` followed by hundreds of `[Rcon: Summoned new Minecart]`; counted 239 minecarts within 64 blocks of that chunk vs 8 near spawn. 4) Declared incident. 5) `forceload remove -560 -352` (chunk unloaded immediately so the first kill found nothing); killed the 5 displaced minecarts at exactly 0,-60,0. 6) Temporarily re-added the forceload, `kill @e[type=minecart,distance=..96]` positioned at the chunk -> 301 flood minecarts removed; verified no minecarts and no other non-player entities remained there; removed the temporary forceload again. 7) Verified `forceload query` -> none; watched ~90 s: TPS 20.0, MSPT 13-17, entities back to baseline 24 (incl. the 3 pre-existing spawn-area minecarts, untouched), chunks loaded 739, no further RCON summon activity. No restart, no bans, no files changed.
report.residual_risk: The source of the RCON commands was not identified or blocked — RCON (127.0.0.1:25621) remains enabled and whoever/whatever holds the password could repeat the forceload+summon pattern; recommend rotating the RCON password and auditing local processes/scripts with RCON access. The 5 flood minecarts I accidentally teleported to 0,-60,0 were removed, but briefly existed at spawn. Chunk [-35,-22] itself was left as-is (no block changes inspected/made).
